entities.name: African Christian Democratic Party
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
The African Christian Democratic Party (ACDP), founded in South Africa in 1993 by Reverend Kenneth Meshoe just before the first democratic elections, is South Africa's principal Christian democratic party — combining conservative Christian social values (opposing abortion, pornography, and same-sex marriage) with a pro-free market economic stance and a political history of consistent, if small, parliamentary representation since 1994.

The ACDP emerged as South Africa transitioned from apartheid to democracy, carving a niche as a party for South African Christians — primarily evangelical Protestants — who found the ANC's social liberalism (particularly its support for abortion rights from 1996) unacceptable but were also committed to racial reconciliation and rejected the racial politics of Afrikaner nationalist parties. Meshoe, a Pentecostal pastor, built the party on a Christian moral platform explicitly rejecting both apartheid (which he condemned as un-Christian) and the ANC's moral and governance failures.

The ACDP has consistently won 1-3% of the national vote and maintains parliamentary representation, distinguishing it from many similar small parties that have disappeared. Its longevity reflects the significant size of South Africa's evangelical Christian community (particularly among Colored and Black Pentecostal/charismatic communities) and Meshoe's personal political brand. The party has opposed same-sex marriage legislation, called for stronger anti-corruption measures, and positioned itself as a 'clean governance' alternative to the ANC's corruption — a positioning that has gained traction as ANC governance failures accumulated.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The African Christian Democratic Party — South Africa's principal Christian democratic party, consistently represented in parliament since 1994, and carving a stable niche for evangelical Christians in post-apartheid democracy — demonstrates the enduring relevance of faith-based political parties in diverse democracies.
